brief.title: Launching the Neighbourhood Heat Pilot
brief.dek: A six-month operating plan for a small council pilot to test a repeatable model for cooling public streets.
brief.thesis: The pilot aims to develop a repeatable model for cooling public streets, focusing on measurable outcomes and a costed plan for potential city-wide implementation.

claims.text: The pilot covers four streets, two schools, and one transport interchange.
claims.label: streets

claims.text: The pilot will track surface temperature, canopy cover, rain interception, complaints, and maintenance hours.
A traffic-light review at month five decides whether to continue the pilot.
claims.label: month

claims.text: The final report should fit on one page and include a clear recommendation.
The council wants to test a repeatable model for cooling public streets before committing to a city-wide programme.

relationships.summary: The pilot follows a five-phase sequence from planning to review.
The pilot timeline outlines key milestones and owners over six months.

risks.risk: Community opposition to tree pits or parking loss.
risks.mitigation: publish trade-offs and co-design two sites.
baseline sensors before planting and two control streets.

brief.bottom_line: The neighbourhood heat pilot is designed to create a repeatable, costed model for urban cooling, with clear phases, success measures, and risk mitigations.
